column1: # The level 1 swipe corpus (bead tla-7xql.4, epic tla-7xql).
# 144 items in three templates, described in swipe/level1/TEMPLATES.tsv.
# Every item pins a STATE and asks a question about it, so unlike level 0 it
# shows a model screen. swipe/level1/render.sh builds that screen and
# swipe/level1/bake.sh measures the verdict.
# Rows are tab-delimited and carry the literal marker ITEM in field 1, so
# prose in this file can never be read as data. Read rows with awk -F'\t' or
# cut, never with IFS=$'\t' read: tab is IFS whitespace, so a run of tabs
# collapses and an empty field vanishes.
# AN ITEM ROW. Thirteen fields, in order. Fields 1 to 11 keep their level 0
# meanings so harness/swipe/stemblind.sh reads this table with --items and no
# code change, and 12 and 13 are what a pinned rung adds:
#    1  marker      the literal ITEM
#    2  id          L1-<template>-<nn>, stable, never renumbered
#    3  template    E1, E2 or E3, resolving to a TEMPLATES.tsv row
#    4  ask         the tag shown WITH the question: enabled, terminal or
#                   implies. It names which of the epic's question kinds the
#                   line is and it does NOT determine the answer
#    5  kind        the item's own kind: true, false, vacuous, illformed,
#                   wronglevel or unparsed. The reader never sees it
#    6  swipe       right, left or down. Derived from field 5 by the bake
#    7  rc          the exit code of the INVARIANT run. Written by the bake
#    8  pin_states  how many states the pin admits. AUTHORED and then
#                   confirmed by the bake's postcondition. A - means 1
#    9  claim       the single line the reader answers
#   10  vacuity     a level 1 witness that the claim is vacuous, or -
#   11  flash       the one line shown after the swipe, always present. On a
#                   false, vacuous, illformed, wronglevel or unparsed item it
#                   is the correction. On a true item it is the reason the
#                   claim holds, because there is nothing to correct about a
#                   true statement. Frank ruled on 2026-10-18
#   12  model       the reading/ module the item is about
#   13  pin         the pinned state, written as a TLA+ conjunction. The bake
#                   uses it verbatim as Ini and render.sh splits it on /\
#   awk -F'\t' '$1 == "ITEM" && $12 == "Brackets"' swipe/level1/ITEMS.tsv
#   grep '^ITEM' swipe/level1/ITEMS.tsv | cut -f5,12 | sort | uniq -c
# FIELDS 6 AND 7 ARE OWNED BY swipe/level1/bake.sh. Do not hand-edit them.
# Field 5 is the author's PREDICTION and the bake is there to contradict it.
# Over E1 it contradicted six of the forty-eight. Over E2 and E3 it
# contradicted none of the ninety-six, and that number is worth as much
# suspicion as a high one until you know what bought it: bead tla-7xql.13
# drove 96 probe runs through a scratch copy of the same channel before any
# row was written, so the contradictions happened at authoring time instead.
# THERE IS NO SECOND EXIT CODE HERE, and that is the first thing a level 0
# reader will look for. Level 0 stores a PAIR because ASSUME exits 10 both
# when the claim is false and when it fails to evaluate, so one number cannot
# split them. The level 1 INVARIANT channel is already five-valued: 0 holds,
# 12 false, 75 does not evaluate, 76 is not a state predicate at all, 150 does
# not parse. One number says which.
# ROW 76 IS THE ONE THIS TEMPLATE EXISTS FOR. TLC's message is "The invariant
# Claim is not a state predicate (one with no primes or temporal operators)",
# and a reader who writes Pop where they mean ENABLED Pop has asked whether a
# STEP holds at a STATE. The bead's own words are that people conflate "the
# guard is true" with "the action can fire"; this is that conflation one layer
# further out, and TLC names it exactly. The kind is called wronglevel.
# THE PIN MUST SATISFY THE MODEL'S OWN TYPE INVARIANT AND NEED NOT BE
# REACHABLE. Nothing in the mechanization constrains a pin: a pin of open = 5
# violates Brackets' own Surplus invariant and ENABLED Pop still reads rc 0,
# because the generated .cfg names Claim and nothing else. TypeOK is the
# model's own statement of what a well-formed state is and it costs one TLC
# run. Reachability costs a model check and would cut the item space hard, and
# ENABLED is a question about a state rather than about a history. CENTRAL
# TOOK THIS RULE AND FRANK HAS NOT RULED ON IT.
# FIELD 8 IS A HAZARD AND NOT BOOKKEEPING. Ini is a predicate rather than an
# assignment, so it may admit more than one state, and then INVARIANT Claim
# asks whether the claim holds at EVERY state it admits. Measured:
# text = <<>> /\ open \in 0..1 with ENABLED Pop reads 12, because the claim
# splits across the two states. Several items pin more than one state on
# purpose: Handover and Key over a set of model values, Matching over a
# symmetric family, Key over the proper nonempty subsets of Staff. The bake
# confirms the count with a POSTCONDITION, so a pin that admits more states
# than its author thought reddens rather than shipping a different question.
# A MULTI-STATE PIN IS A CHOICE AND NOT A CONSTRAINT, AND THIS FILE SAID THE
# OPPOSITE UNTIL 2026-10-18. The old wording ran: Handover's
# CONSTANT Site = {s1, s2, s3} is a set of MODEL VALUES, a model value is not
# an identifier the pin module can name, Ini == holder = s1 comes back rc 150,
# so holder \in Site is the only pin Handover has. The first three clauses are
# measured and the conclusion does not follow. Declare a constant in the pin
# module and bind it in the .cfg:
#   CONSTANT H                      CONSTANT Site = {s1, s2, s3}
#   Ini == holder = H /\ want = TRUE         H = s1
# Measured rc 0, one state. Corrected in swipe/README.md at commit 8148330 and
# here by bead tla-7xql.13, which found the sentence still standing in this
# file. bake.sh generates its CONSTANT block from the model's own .cfg and has
# no field for an extra one, so no shipped item uses the shape yet. What it
# changes is what an author sizing a new template believes, and most of the
# models E2 and E3 draw on carry model values.
# A PIN MUST ALSO BE ENUMERABLE, which is a separate hazard with the same
# symptom. TLC generates initial states from Ini rather than filtering them,
# so a pin that only RECOGNIZES a state rather than constructing one fails.
# Measured 2026-10-18: Ini == hook = FALSE /\ inside # {} /\ inside # Staff
# reads rc 75 with 0 states, and so does the CLAIM module over the same pin,
# which the channel would otherwise read as illformed. The auxiliary run is
# what tells a broken pin from a claim that does not denote.
# ITEMS ARE AUTHORED IN MATCHED GROUPS, which is what keeps the stem-blind
# gate green. The unit is either a four, one item of each of four kinds built
# from one idea, or a pair, a true and a false built from one idea. Six fours
# and twelve pairs is 48, and it lands the mix at 18 true, 18 false and 12
# down without anybody counting. Rows sit in their authoring groups so a
# reviewer sees a matched pair side by side, and ids are never renumbered.
# E2 AND E3 ADD A SECOND DEVICE ON TOP OF THE GROUPS: SIX PAIRS PER TEMPLATE
# CARRY THE SAME CLAIM TEXT AT TWO PINS WITH OPPOSITE ANSWERS. That is the
# one construction a surface classifier cannot be right about, because the
# surface is identical and the labels differ, and it is cheap to build once
# the pins are in hand. It also says the rung's own lesson to a reader who
# meets both halves: the claim does not decide, the state does.
# THE SWIPE MIX IS LEVEL 0'S AND THE KIND MIX IS NOT. Right is 18 of 48 in
# every template, so the base rate is 0.3750 and the power table in
# swipe/README.md transfers unchanged. That argument is about the SWIPE mix,
# which is why it carries. The kind mix under down does not: level 0 splits
# 12 into 6 vacuous, 5 illformed and 1 unparsed over five kinds, and this
# rung has six kinds to place.
#   template   vacuous  illformed  wronglevel  unparsed
# E1's split is the baseline and the two deviations are each one item, each
# in the direction its own subject supplies. E2 is about quantifiers and an
# empty range is the quantifier's own way of answering without looking at the
# action, so vacuity is native there. E3 is about terminal states and writing
# ~(Push \/ Pop) where ~ENABLED (Push \/ Pop) was meant is the mistake that
# template exists to catch, so wronglevel is native there. A template that
# supplies no kind more naturally should hold E1's split rather than invent a
# reason to move.
# A CLAIM MAY ONLY NAME A DEFINITION THE SCREEN SHOWS. Decision D7 withholds
# Init, Next and Spec, so a terminal item asks ~ENABLED (Push \/ Pop) and
# never ~ENABLED Next: a reader cannot evaluate a name they have not been
# given. swipe/level1/render.sh --list-shown is the authority and
# harness/test-swipe-enabled.sh asserts it over every row.
# NO ITEM MAY DEPEND ON \div WITH A NEGATIVE DIVIDEND. TLC 2026.07.31.184830
# breaks the contract its own Naturals.tla states. The note in
# swipe/level0/ITEMS.tsv carries the measurement and bead tla-7n7e is open on
# it. No claim or pin here uses \div at all.
# FIELD 11 IS NOT OPTIONAL. L2 on the epic: a falsehood is reproduced later at
# .19 with no feedback, .15 with a bare verdict and .04 with the verdict plus
# the correction. The gate rejects a blank one and a stub.

column1: # TEMPLATE E2 — one quantifier changes the question (bead tla-7xql.13)
# E1 spends five of its forty-eight items on a parameterized action. This
# template spends all of them, because the three shapes a reader meets look
# alike and are not: \E p \in S : ENABLED A(p) asks for one witness,
# \A p \in S : ENABLED A(p) asks for every member, and ENABLED A(c) asks
# about one argument and says nothing about the rest.
# SIX PAIRS CARRY THE SAME CLAIM TEXT AT TWO PINS WITH OPPOSITE ANSWERS, and
# that is the template's defense against a reader who answers from the line
# alone. L1-E2-11 and L1-E2-14 are both \A p \in Staff : ENABLED Take(p), one
# right and one left. So are 12 and 13, 17 and 22, 24 and 27, 31 and 36, and
# 37 against E3's matching pins.
# THE RANGE MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE QUANTIFIER, which is the half nobody
# writes down. L1-E2-15 and L1-E2-16 are the same quantifier over the same
# action at the same state, and the only difference is inside against Staff.
# THE KIND MIX UNDER down MOVES BY ONE FROM E1, and the reason is this
# template's subject. E1 splits 12 into 4 vacuous, 3 illformed, 3 wronglevel
# and 2 unparsed. E2 splits it 5, 3, 2, 2. An empty range is the quantifier's
# own way of answering without looking at the action, so vacuity is not a
# borrowed kind here, it is the failure mode the subject supplies. The epic's
# bead names empty-range vacuity as living naturally in this template.
# A PIN HAS TO BE ENUMERABLE AND NOT MERELY TRUE OF A STATE. Measured on
# 2026-10-18: Ini == hook = FALSE /\ inside # {} /\ inside # Staff comes back
# rc 75 with 0 states, because TLC generates initial states from the predicate
# rather than filtering them. The pin at L1-E2-15 says the same thing as
# inside \in {s \in SUBSET Staff : s # {} /\ s # Staff} and that one
# enumerates. A broken pin reads rc 75 on the CLAIM too, which the channel
# would call illformed, so the bake's auxiliary run is what tells the two
# apart.

column1: # TEMPLATE E3 — stuck, finished, or only this one action (bead tla-7xql.13)
# 79 of the 337 published configurations in this project's corpus survey set
# CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE on purpose, so telling a stopped run from a wedged one
# is a working skill rather than a footnote. E1 asks it seven times and every
# one of those models has a single reason for stopping.
# THE ASK HERE IS THAT THE REASONS DIFFER. Ledger stops because every tally
# has reached Max and because the sparse map carries no key, which are two
# unrelated facts about one state. Tickets stops because every player already
# holds a ticket and because none of those tickets is the one being served.
# Key stops because the key is off its hook and because nobody is inside.
# A reader who checks one guard and stops has answered a different question,
# and the false items are built so that checking one guard gives the wrong
# answer.
# FOUR PINS ARE UNREACHABLE AND TYPE CORRECT, which is the pin rule doing
# work rather than being tolerated. Matching's terminal state violates its own
# Involution invariant, and Key's violates Hooked. Neither model can reach a
# terminal state at all without them, so under a reachability rule this
# template would have had no true terminal item on either model. CENTRAL TOOK
# THE RULE AND FRANK HAS NOT RULED ON IT.
# THE KIND MIX UNDER down MOVES BY ONE FROM E1 IN THE OTHER DIRECTION FROM
# E2. E1 splits 12 into 4 vacuous, 3 illformed, 3 wronglevel and 2 unparsed.
# E3 splits it 3, 3, 4, 2. Writing ~(Push \/ Pop) where ~ENABLED (Push \/ Pop)
# was meant is this template's own mistake rather than a borrowed one, and two

# reaches only the first arm.

# right and one left, and so are 09 and 14, 15 and 20, 23 and 28, 35 and 40,
# 41 and 44. The claim alone decides nothing at this rung.
